paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD is worth every bit of that shouting. The writer says His word is upright and all His work is trustworthy (Psalm 33:4). By His word the heavens were made, and 'For He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm' (Psalm 33:6, 9). When the One who speaks stars into place says something, it STANDS, and that's why this psalm opens with a harp and a shout of joy.

So where do you put your hope when the pressure is on? The writer says no king is saved by his vast army, and a horse is a vain hope for salvation (Psalm 33:16-17). Baker, my mustache can lift a full cookie box, and it never once got me out of that drawer. Plans, muscles and big numbers all run out, but 'The counsel of the LORD stands forever' (Psalm 33:11).

And here's the part I love most. The eyes of the LORD are on those who fear Him, on those whose hope is in His loving devotion (Psalm 33:18). Our soul waits for Him, and He is our help and our shield (Psalm 33:20). So when you're waiting, don't stare at the oven window like I do. Trust Him, rejoice in Him, and pray the psalm's last words with me: 'May Your loving devotion rest on us, O LORD, as we put our hope in You' (Psalm 33:22).
